title: Tenant isolation validator and Terraform plan guard for RBAC bootstrapping
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: automating safe RBAC bootstrapping for Private deployments uncovered two recurring risks: (1) accidental tenant role grants during initial bootstrap and upgrades, and (2) drift between Helm/Terraform manifests and the installer runtime that can cause privilege escalation on upgrade. This PR introduces a validator that runs during installer preflight and a Terraform plan guard that blocks applies if tenant-isolation regressions are detected. Goals: make tenant scoping explicit, fail fast on RBAC drift, provide clear remediation guidance, and keep upgrade/rollback paths recovery-friendly. Changes include a lightweight JSONSchema-based validator embedded in the installer preflight, a terraform plan hook that runs a policy evaluation step using the same policy bundle used by the installer, and a set of automated remediation diffs suggested as part of the plan output. Checklist: 1) add validator module and integrate with preflight; 2) add terraform plan guard wrapper script and CI job; 3) update Helm chart RBAC templates to emit tenant-labels and annotation metadata used by validator; 4) include detailed upgrade notes and rollback playbook references; 5) add unit/e2e tests and testdata for multi-tenant scenarios. Rollout plan: initial opt-in using HELM_VALUES flag enable_rbac_validator=false by default; enable flag for beta customers and progressively roll into default after telemetry shows zero false positives. Reasoning: we decouple detection (validator) from enforcement (plan guard) so operators can preview and fix with suggested diffs before enforcement is enabled. Backwards compatibility: validator tolerates older chart shapes and includes a permissive mode to avoid blocking older customers. Risk: false positives during complex legacy role mappings; mitigations described in release_notes and upgrade docs.

changes_summary: Added a JSONSchema validator and policy rules to detect tenant-scoped role regressions; integrated validator into installer preflight; added a terraform plan wrapper that evaluates generated plan against the policy bundle and exits non-zero if tenant-isolation issues are found; updated Helm templates to emit tenant-labels and annotations used by the validator; added unit and e2e tests; CI job rbac-plan-guard added. Default behavior is permissive to prevent customer impact; enforcement is gated by enable_rbac_validator/plan_guard flags.

release_notes: Operator-facing: Introduce tenant isolation validator and terraform plan guard. Default mode is permissive; enforcement can be enabled via enable_rbac_validator and enable_plan_guard flags. The plan guard will block terraform apply if tenant-isolation regressions are detected when enforcement is on. Includes suggested remediation diffs. See docs/upgrade/tenant-rbac-validator.md for migration and rollback playbook.
upgrade_instructions: To opt into enforcement: 1) Set enable_rbac_validator=true and enable_plan_guard=false and run terraform plan to surface issues; 2) apply suggested remediation patches or run the included fixer script; 3) enable enable_plan_guard=true in a maintenance window behind operator approval; 4) Monitor validator.dashboard for hits and revert enable_plan_guard if needed.
rollback_notes: Rollback path: if enforcement blocks a necessary upgrade, flip enable_plan_guard=false, re-run terraform apply, and then follow the remediation guidance to bring RBAC resources into compliant shape. The playbook contains kubectl commands to reconcile legacy role labels and a script to patch clusterrolebindings safely.
notes_for_sre: Added observability hooks: installer emits rbac_validator.hit events with labels (tenant, severity, rule_id) and a sample_count metric. SREs should watch rbac.validator.alerts in the Redwood Console, initially routed to oncall-team-rbac for the canary period.
